# externals.io

> externals.io is a read-only web mirror of php.internals, the mailing list where PHP core developers discuss RFCs and the development of the PHP language. Emails are synchronized from the official archive every 15 minutes and grouped into threads.

- Every email has a number: the NNTP article number in the official archive (`https://news-web.php.net/php.internals/{number}`).
- A thread is identified by the number of its first email. Requesting a reply's number redirects to the thread root.
- RFC discussions usually have `[RFC]`, `[VOTE]` or `[DISCUSSION]` in the subject. The RFCs themselves live at https://wiki.php.net/rfc and are imported every hour (see "RFCs" below).
- The site is read-only: to take part in a discussion, reply by email to internals@lists.php.net.
- Everything below is public and needs no authentication.

## Threads

- [Thread as Markdown](https://externals.io/message/{number}.md): the thread (messages in chronological order) as Markdown. Sending `Accept: text/markdown` to `/message/{number}` returns the same content. Long threads are split in pages of 25 messages (`?page=N`, the header gives the page count and the next page URL); a reply's number redirects to the page that contains it.
- [Thread as HTML](https://externals.io/message/{number}): the thread page for humans.
- [Latest threads](https://externals.io/?page=1): threads by latest activity, 20 per page (`?page=N`).
- [Top threads](https://externals.io/top?page=1): most upvoted threads of the last month.

## RFCs

- [RFCs as Markdown](https://externals.io/rfc.md): all RFCs of https://wiki.php.net/rfc grouped by status (in voting, under discussion, draft, accepted, implemented by PHP version, declined, withdrawn, inactive, obsolete). Sending `Accept: text/markdown` to `/rfc` returns the same content.
- [RFC as Markdown](https://externals.io/rfc/{slug}.md): an RFC (the slug is the wiki page name, e.g. `pipe-operator-v3`) with its status, its votes (results and voters), the threads that discuss it, and its full text.
- An RFC is linked to a thread when the first email of the thread links to the RFC page, or when the RFC page links to the thread. Thread pages list their RFCs.

## Search

- [Search as Markdown](https://externals.io/search.md?q={query}): full-text search over email subjects and content, with links to the Markdown threads.
- [Search as HTML](https://externals.io/search?q={query}&page=1): the same results for humans.
- All search endpoints accept `page=N` (20 results per page) and `since` / `until` dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Results are individual emails, each with the number of its thread (`threadNumber` in JSON): several results can belong to the same thread.

## JSON API

Meant for agents and personal tools: please don't bulk download the archive through it.

- [API index](https://externals.io/api): lists the endpoints and their parameters.
- [List threads](https://externals.io/api/threads?sort=latest&page=1): `sort` is `latest` or `top`, 20 threads per page.
- [Get a thread](https://externals.io/api/threads/{number}): the thread and its messages, with message content as Markdown. Messages are paginated like the Markdown thread (`?page=N`, see `meta` and `links`).
- [Search](https://externals.io/api/search?q={query}&page=1): search results as JSON.
- [List RFCs](https://externals.io/api/rfcs?status=voting): all RFCs in the order of the wiki index, optionally filtered by `status`.
- [Get an RFC](https://externals.io/api/rfcs/{slug}): an RFC with its votes, its threads, and its text as Markdown. `/api/threads/{number}` lists the RFCs of a thread in `rfcs`.

## Feeds

- [Latest emails (RSS)](https://externals.io/rss)
- [Latest RFC threads (RSS)](https://externals.io/rss-rfc)
- [Sitemap](https://externals.io/sitemap.xml): every thread with its last update date.

## Optional

- [Original archive](https://news-web.php.net/php.internals): the official php.internals archive on the PHP NNTP server.
- [Source code](https://github.com/mnapoli/externals): externals.io is open source.
